notes.title: SteamVR Home: Trophies, Artwork, and More
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5519564/093550779914d1aec29f69ef429bb7f4324a6bd3.jpg[/img]
Today we are updating SteamVR Home with new content, more ways to customize your home space, built in Steam Audio technology, and more. These features are available by opting into [b]SteamVR Beta[/b]*.

[video=autoplay preload loop poster=http://media.steampowered.com/apps/250820/announcements/september_update/trophy_thumb.jpg]http://media.steampowered.com/apps/250820/announcements/september_update/trophy.webm?v=1[/video]

[h1]Trophies[/h1]
Players can now bring Trophies that represent games from their SteamVR Library into SteamVR Home. These Trophies will upgrade as the player completes achievements and crafts badges for the game. In addition, they give players access to game details and a quick way to launch the game. Players can use these as physical shortcuts, decorate their space and show off their progress in their favorite VR games.


[video=autoplay preload loop poster=http://media.steampowered.com/apps/250820/announcements/september_update/screenshot_thumb.jpg]http://media.steampowered.com/apps/250820/announcements/september_update/screenshot.webm?v=1[/video]

[h1]Screenshots and Artwork[/h1]
Players can now place screenshots and artwork from their favorite games in-world. These can be images the player has uploaded, or popular content from the community. These panels can be spawned from the Things menu in the Content Browser, or from the Community Wall in the default SteamVR Home environment. To adjust the location of a screenshot or art panel, grab the edge with the trigger button. To remove them, use the Multi-Tool.

[h1]SteamVR Panels[/h1]
Players can now place the SteamVR panels (Recent Apps, Friends List, and Rooms List) in any location, and in any environment. This means any environment can be made into a home space with quick access to friends, rooms, and games. Similar to screenshots and artwork, these panels can be spawned from the Things menu in the Content Browser, moved by grabbing the edge, and removed with the Multi-Tool.

[h1]Steam Audio[/h1]
Steam Audio is now integrated into SteamVR Home and enabled by default on positional sounds, making it easy to integrate immersive audio into your workshop environments. Steam Audio binaurally renders direct sound using HRTFs to accurately model the direction of a sound source relative to the listener. Players will now get an impression of the height of the sound source, as well as whether the source is in front of or behind them. See the SteamVR developer wiki for more information on adding sounds to your environment.

[video=autoplay preload loop poster=http://media.steampowered.com/apps/250820/announcements/september_update/boxing_ring_thumb.jpg]http://media.steampowered.com/apps/250820/announcements/september_update/boxing_ring.webm?v=1[/video]

[h1]Boxing Ring[/h1]
For this update we've created a new SteamVR Home environment to subscribe to and explore. Visit the Boxing Ring and train on punching bags, lift weights, or compete with the training bot in the ring. See how quickly you can take the training bot down!

[h1]Tutorials[/h1]
We've also updated the SteamVR Home Developer wiki with two new tutorials for creators and creators-to-be:[list]
    [*][url=https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/SteamVR/Environments/Introduction]Introduction[/url] - An overview of the SteamVR Home engine and development tools, for everyone from beginners to veterans.
    [*][url=https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/SteamVR/Environments/Environment_Tutorial:_Hammer_and_Basic_Lighting]Hammer and Basic Lighting[/url] - Learn how to construct an an environment from basic geometry and set up simple lighting. notes.title: SteamVR Home: Trophies, Artwork, and More
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5519564/093550779914d1aec29f69ef429bb7f4324a6bd3.jpg[/img]
Today we are updating SteamVR Home with new content, more ways to customize your home space, built in Steam Audio technology, and more. These features are available by opting into [b]SteamVR Beta[/b]*.

[video=autoplay preload loop poster=http://media.steampowered.com/apps/250820/announcements/september_update/trophy_thumb.jpg]http://media.steampowered.com/apps/250820/announcements/september_update/trophy.webm?v=1[/video]

[h1]Trophies[/h1]
Players can now bring Trophies that represent games from their SteamVR Library into SteamVR Home. These Trophies will upgrade as the player completes achievements and crafts badges for the game. In addition, they give players access to game details and a quick way to launch the game. Players can use these as physical shortcuts, decorate their space and show off their progress in their favorite VR games.


[video=autoplay preload loop poster=http://media.steampowered.com/apps/250820/announcements/september_update/screenshot_thumb.jpg]http://media.steampowered.com/apps/250820/announcements/september_update/screenshot.webm?v=1[/video]

[h1]Screenshots and Artwork[/h1]
Players can now place screenshots and artwork from their favorite games in-world. These can be images the player has uploaded, or popular content from the community. These panels can be spawned from the Things menu in the Content Browser, or from the Community Wall in the default SteamVR Home environment. To adjust the location of a screenshot or art panel, grab the edge with the trigger button. To remove them, use the Multi-Tool.

[h1]SteamVR Panels[/h1]
Players can now place the SteamVR panels (Recent Apps, Friends List, and Rooms List) in any location, and in any environment. This means any environment can be made into a home space with quick access to friends, rooms, and games. Similar to screenshots and artwork, these panels can be spawned from the Things menu in the Content Browser, moved by grabbing the edge, and removed with the Multi-Tool.

[h1]Steam Audio[/h1]
Steam Audio is now integrated into SteamVR Home and enabled by default on positional sounds, making it easy to integrate immersive audio into your workshop environments. Steam Audio binaurally renders direct sound using HRTFs to accurately model the direction of a sound source relative to the listener. Players will now get an impression of the height of the sound source, as well as whether the source is in front of or behind them. See the SteamVR developer wiki for more information on adding sounds to your environment.

[video=autoplay preload loop poster=http://media.steampowered.com/apps/250820/announcements/september_update/boxing_ring_thumb.jpg]http://media.steampowered.com/apps/250820/announcements/september_update/boxing_ring.webm?v=1[/video]

[h1]Boxing Ring[/h1]
For this update we've created a new SteamVR Home environment to subscribe to and explore. Visit the Boxing Ring and train on punching bags, lift weights, or compete with the training bot in the ring. See how quickly you can take the training bot down!

[h1]Tutorials[/h1]
We've also updated the SteamVR Home Developer wiki with two new tutorials for creators and creators-to-be:[list]
    [*][url=https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/SteamVR/Environments/Introduction]Introduction[/url] - An overview of the SteamVR Home engine and development tools, for everyone from beginners to veterans.
    [*][url=https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/SteamVR/Environments/Environment_Tutorial:_Hammer_and_Basic_Lighting]Hammer and Basic Lighting[/url] - Learn how to construct an an environment from basic geometry and set up simple lighting. The first in a series which will end with a SteamVR Home environment depicting a real place.
[/list]
[h1]Other Updates[/h1]
In addition to the new features above, we've added a slew of new furniture and increased the visual fidelity of existing props, tools, and furniture. Customizing your home space will be even easier now, as we've improved the way props and furniture are positioned and placed in-world. 

We look forward to seeing how you will take advantage of these new features to customize your spaces. Let us know what you think in the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/250820/discussions/6/]discussion boards[/url].

notes.title: SteamVR Updated (1504061330)
notes.content:
SteamVR has been updated with the following changes:

General:
[list]
[*]Supports OpenVR SDK 1.0.10 and lower.
[*]Fix for timeout loop that occurred in some situations with wireless headsets.
[*]Fixes a resource leak for SetOverlayRaw or SetOverlayFromFile.
[*]Fixes a bug that caused trackpad touch coordinates to jump to the center at the beginning of a swipe.
[/list]

Windows:
[list]
[*] Fixed intermittent GPU timestamp inaccuracy for Vulkan applications.
[*]Fixed issue that kept game theater from starting reliably
[/list]

macOS:
[list]
[*]Resolves multiple memory leaks when apps are MRC (lacking @autoreleasepool) instead of ARC
[*]Corrects installation of steamvr helper ipcserver service
[*]Corrects launchd configuration for shared resource manager (ipcserver_vr)
[*]Improves Xcode VR frame debugger integration
[*]Fixes configuration paths preventing launch on a clean macOS install
[*]Allows system to enter sleep/suspend when VR is inactive, supporting reduced power consumption
[/list]

Linux:
[list]
[*]Improved performance of OpenGL clients if EXT_memory_object_fd is available
[*]Flipped over to the KHR version of external_memory and external_semaphore Vulkan extensions; recent RADV or NVIDIA driver 381.26.08 is now required
[*]Fixed symbol regression
[/list]

notes.title: SteamVR Updated (1499136050)
notes.content:
SteamVR has been updated with the following changes. This is the most recent beta build from July 5th.

General:
[list]
[*][macOS] Fixes reporting of correct HMD eGPU to application
[*][macOS] reduces idle cpu overhead and removes extraneous vrcompositor and vrserver dock icons
[*][Windows] Fixes crash when submitting dynamically size-adjusted render target for DX12-based applications
[*]Corrected the error that is reported when no hardware is present. It was reporting error 208 which implies that the problem is HDMI related when it should have been reporting error 108, the generic “HMD not found” error.
[*]Fixed bugs related to “pipe disconnections” in certain games on certain user machines. One way this would manifest is that haptic feedback would stop working, but sometimes it appeared as general instability in SteamVR.
[*]Trackpad data from Vive Tracker external pins is passed through without filtering.
[/list]


SteamVR Home:
[list]
[*]Fixed a case where SteamVR Home would come up instead when launching something from the dashboard.
[*]Improved behavior when restarting SteamVR so SteamVR Home will run as appropriate.
[*]Fixed equipped tools not ghosting when within another player’s personal bubble
[*]Now hiding the Home version of your hands when the SteamVR controllers are rendered (when the dashboard is up) 
[*]Fixed crash when launching Hammer from SteamVR Workshop Tools 
[*]Material tweaks on some avatar heads
[*]Fixed vertex normals on various hairpieces
[*]Promo items are now called out in the Content Browser
[*]Updated localization
[*]Visual improvements in the default "Summit Pavilion" map. (e.g. added a maple tree to the patio, improved lighting, better fog tuning)
[*]Removed some unused assets to reduce install size
[*]Fixed vertex normal on some furniture assets
[/list]


Compositor:
[list]
[*]The “vrcompositor.exe” process will now use significantly less CPU and GPU when the running application is SteamVR Home and the user’s headset is idle. 
[/list]

Oculus:
[list]
[*]The Rift HMD now sends k_EButton_ProximitySensor events when the proximity sensor is triggered.
[/list]

Vive Tracker Firmware:
[list]
[*]Fixed a bug where the trackpad button would not update correctly via accessory POGO pins.
[/list]

notes.title: Introducing SteamVR Collectibles
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5519564/9c5dd96a0bf8bd3aa32e2b04bc3e0b6296a283ea.png[/img]

Today we are adding SteamVR Collectibles to SteamVR Home – items from other Steam titles that can be unlocked and used in SteamVR Home. We’ve partnered with a few VR game developers to create a set of items using characters and props from their titles, and they look amazing. This first wave of Collectibles will be made available to players based on ownership or playtime of the following titles: 
[list]
[*]Job Simulator
[*]Fantastic Contraption
[*]Space Pirate Trainer
[*]Audioshield
[*]The Gallery – Episode 1: Call of the Starseed
[*]Arizona Sunshine
[*]Onward
[*]AirMech Command
[*]Serious Sam: The Last Hope
[*]Hover Junkers
[*]The Lab
[*]Dota 2
[/list]
We think Collectibles will be a fun way for players to show their love for a game - whether it be by decorating their place or by modifying their avatar. This first wave is just the beginning and we’re excited to see where this will lead.

Let us know what you think in the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/250820/discussions/6/]discussion boards[/url].

Today we are adding SteamVR Collectibles to SteamVR Home – items from other Steam titles that can be unlocked and used in SteamVR Home. We’ve partnered with a few VR game developers to create a set of items using characters and props from their titles, and they look amazing. This first wave of Collectibles will be made available to players based on ownership or playtime of the following titles: 
[list]
[*]Job Simulator
[*]Fantastic Contraption
[*]Space Pirate Trainer
[*]Audioshield
[*]The Gallery – Episode 1: Call of the Starseed
[*]Arizona Sunshine
[*]Onward
[*]AirMech Command
[*]Serious Sam: The Last Hope
[*]Hover Junkers
[*]The Lab
[*]Dota 2
[/list]
We think Collectibles will be a fun way for players to show their love for a game - whether it be by decorating their place or by modifying their avatar. This first wave is just the beginning and we’re excited to see where this will lead.

Let us know what you think in the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/250820/discussions/6/]discussion boards[/url].

notes.title: SteamVR Updated (1496873977)
notes.content:
SteamVR has been updated with the following changes:

[b]SteamVR:[/b]
[list]
[*]Added SteamVR Home Beta.  For more details, see the following announcement: http://steamcommunity.com/games/250820/announcements/detail/1256913672017157095)
[*]Redesigned parts of the SteamVR dashboard, including adding an explicit Go Home button (if opted out of SteamVR Home Beta, this becomes a Quit App button) 
[*]Fixed issue where the time would sometimes show up in the wrong place in the Dashboard.
[*]Fixed issue that allowed stale SteamVR apps to block SteamVR from starting up.
[*]Fixed issue with SteamVR status window showing a failure when launching certain apps from Steam before starting SteamVR itself.
[*]Removed enableDistortion user preference
[*]Fixed startup crash in Battlezone on DX12 when Advanced Supersampling is enabled
[*]Fixed an issue that caused some Revive games to not render in the HMD. 
[*]Fixed issue that caused Steam to think an app was still running. This would happen when the app started SteamVR as part of its own startup process.
[*]Fixed case where some applications would fail to connect to SteamVR when launched from outside of Steam.
[*]Fix for negative integers in settings.
[*]Fix for non-pow2 textures failing to load on AMD hardware with mip-map generation enabled.
[*]Fix for finding headset display in extended mode.  (Err=400)
[*]Fixed a problem that sometimes prevented some applications (including Star Trek: Bridge Crew) from starting up when SteamVR Home Beta is enabled.
[*]Fixed IsHmdPresent detection for Oculus devices.
[*]Minor updates to the SteamVR Tutorial.
[/list]

[b]Supersampling[/b]
[list]
[*]Changed the supersample slider to no longer require a restart of SteamVR. Some application may require a restart for the new settings to take, but many existing applications respond correctly without restarting
[*]Added an option to disable image filtering on supersampled renderings
[*]Supersample slider now behaves linearly where 2.0 now means 2.0 times the number of pixels. Previously the slider was applied as a multiplier to width and height, so 2.0 used to mean (2.0 times 2.0 = 4.0) 4.0 the number of pixels. Existing settings will automatically be converted to the new linear scale.
[/list]

[b]MacOS[/b]
[list]
[*]Beta SteamVR support on macOS 10.11.6 and higher. Details about Unity, Unreal, and Firefox support [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/250820/announcements/detail/1256915122285021922]here[/url]
[*]Direct-to-Display (aka Direct Mode) support on macOS High Sierra developer seed with HTC Vive
[*]Dashboard and overlays are currently disabled
[*]Feedback welcome, join the developer community or use the Bug Report / Feature Request menu options
[/list]

[b]Known Issues:[/b]
[list]
[*] SteamVR crash on startup with Kepler-based gpus (e.g GTX 680, 780, Titan Black) using the latest Nvidia drivers.  This can be avoided by rolling back to Nvidia driver v381.89 for now.
https://www.nvidia.com/Download/Find.aspx
[/list]

notes.title: SteamVR for MacOS: Beta Available Now
notes.content:
As part of our efforts to make VR available to developers and players on as many systems as possible, SteamVR for the Mac is now available in beta. The beta comes in tandem with the macOS High Sierra developer seed and hardware news from Apple's 2017 Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC) that helps enable VR on the Mac.
 
SteamVR on the Mac offers players the same 360-degree, room-scale tracking as the Windows and Linux variants.
 
On the development side, we have worked closely with Epic and Unity to make Mac extensions of content built on those engine technologies as simple as possible. Extension tools for those engines, and others, are available as part of this beta.
 
We’ve also worked with Mozilla to help enable WebVR support on Firefox, so macOS-based web developers can start trying out VR.

[h1]To use SteamVR on your Mac[/h1]
[olist]
 [*]Open Steam on your desktop
 [*]Find SteamVR in your Library under Tools
 [*]Right click and go to Properties
 [*]Select the Betas tab and pick SteamVR Beta from the dropdown
[/olist]

[h1]To make something for SteamVR on the Mac[/h1]
[list]
 [*]For more information and access to Unity's updates for SteamVR and macOS go [url=https://blogs.unity3d.com/?p=50112]here[/url]
 [*]Learn more about today's WWDC demo and Unreal Engine support for SteamVR on Mac [url=http://epic.gm/wwdc17]here[/url]
 [*]Instructions for installing Firefox and WebVR samples can be found [url=https://webvr.rocks/firefox]here[/url]
 [*]Download the latest OpenVR Software Development Kit (SDK) [url=https://github.com/ValveSoftware/openvr]here[/url]
[/list]

[h1]System Requirements[/h1]
[list]
 [*]SteamVR for macOS requires Metal graphics support in macOS 10.11.6 or higher and runs best with Metal 2 in the macOS High Sierra developer seed
 [*]An HTC Vive and appropriate connectors for Mac hardware
[/list]

notes.title: Introducing SteamVR Home Beta
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5519564/1cecb6e93ac9069b3fd59cfdb7210595a21e965f.png[/img]

Today we are updating SteamVR with a new home experience that is richer, more interactive, and more social than the existing launch area. SteamVR Home is currently in beta and we welcome your feedback in the discussion boards.

Ever since SteamVR was released last year, we've been steadily adding ways to customize the launch area (where players start when starting up SteamVR). It's been exciting to see the creativity of the community in the diverse environments and backgrounds submitted to the SteamVR Workshop so far. We've also heard loud and clear that creators want the ability to make more detailed home environments, with sound, animation, interaction, and social elements. All of these features and more are now available with the new SteamVR Home update.


[video=autoplay preload loop poster=http://media.steampowered.com/apps/250820/announcements/steamvr_home/steamvr_environments.png]http://media.steampowered.com/apps/250820/announcements/steamvr_home/steamvr_environments.webm?v=1[/video]

[h1]Richer, customizable environments[/h1]
Environments can now be higher resolution and support animation, sound, games, and interactivity. Players can teleport around and explore any of the hundreds of environments created by the community. In addition, players can customize and save their environment with props and drawings, then set it as their default home space.


[video=autoplay preload loop poster=http://media.steampowered.com/apps/250820/announcements/steamvr_home/steamvr_multiplayer.png]http://media.steampowered.com/apps/250820/announcements/steamvr_home/steamvr_multiplayer.webm?v=1[/video]

[h1]Socialize with friends[/h1]
SteamVR Home has social functions built in, making it easier than ever to connect to friends and other players. Invite friends to join you in your home space, or open any environment up to friends or the public. Voice chat with other players, interact with tools and props, and explore different SteamVR environments with others.


[video=autoplay preload loop poster=http://media.steampowered.com/apps/250820/announcements/steamvr_home/steamvr_avatar.png]http://media.steampowered.com/apps/250820/announcements/steamvr_home/steamvr_avatar.webm?v=1[/video]

[h1]Customize your avatar[/h1]
Choose your avatar's head and accessorize it with wearables and props. Additional avatars and wearables can be found by completing quests in other SteamVR environments.
 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5519564/f2146a094792b0d0d11857e30bd7320e2cbdf3f8.png[/img]

[h1]Quick links[/h1]
The default home space includes quick links to your most recently launched VR applications, your Friends list, and open Public or Private rooms. Creators will also have access to these panels and can embed them into any environments they create.
 
[h1]SteamVR Workshop[/h1]
All existing SteamVR backgrounds and environments are being updated today and will still be available for use. Once updated, players will be able to move around, customize the environment, and invite their friends. The hand customization workshop is under active development and will be available soon.

Creators can use SteamVR Workshop Tools to create and submit environments. This application is accessible in the Tools section of the Steam Library. To learn more about how to get started creating an environment from 3D models or photogrammetry, visit the SteamVR Workshop Wiki.

[h1]Destinations[/h1]
If the content of this update seems familiar, good eye! The core functionality for this update comes from one of our other VR applications - Destinations. To learn more about what's happening with Destinations, see [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/453170/announcements/detail/1315462370962473336]this post[/url].

We believe these updates will improve the SteamVR experience for all players. Let us know what you think in the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/250820/discussions/6/]discussion boards[/url].

[i]*If you'd like to opt out of SteamVR Home Beta, go to Settings in the Dashboard (Press the System button and select Settings) and uncheck SteamVR Home Beta.*[/i]

notes.title: Steam Audio for Unreal Engine 4
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27920370/1739643f26e04c63771038b1cd96d6b94a9e3ac4.png[/img]

Today we are excited to announce the first beta release of Steam Audio for Unreal Engine 4. Our plugin now ships with UE4 by default, so you can get started by upgrading to 4.16 Preview 2. This release brings our physically-based sound propagation and HRTF rendering to the UE4 engine, enabling developers to immediately begin creating immersive audio experiences for games and VR. The plugin is free of charge and is not locked to a particular platform or VR device. Users can get started by upgrading to 4.16 Preview 2, then grabbing the documentation from our [url=https://valvesoftware.github.io/steam-audio/downloads.html]downloads page[/url].

The plugin is designed to work with the new audio engine introduced in 4.16. Starting UE4 with the [i]-audiomixer[/i] flag will enable the new engine and give you access to the plugin. The first release is experimental and will benefit greatly from your feedback in the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/596420/discussions/]discussion forums[/url]. You can explore existing issues and report new ones over at our [url=https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-audio/issues]GitHub issues page[/url]. We expect to fix major issues as they arise and provide timely bug fixes as we progress through the beta. Many of the features we've built for the new audio engine together with Epic will be broadly helpful to all third party developers. We encourage developers to explore the plugin's source code to see the new capabilities exposed by the native audio engine.

The Steam Audio plugin for UE4 provides three major pieces of functionality: HRTF filtering with per-source settings, direct-sound occlusion, and physically-based sound propagation.

[h1]HRTF Filtering with Per-Source Settings[/h1]

Two years ago, UE4 introduced support for third party HRTF spatialization. In 4.16, spatialization plugins can customize the behavior of HRTF processing on a per-source basis. Users configure spatialization plugins with [i]Spatialization Plugin Settings[/i] assets. The Steam Audio plugin provides robust HRTF processing and lets users choose between [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/596420/announcements/detail/507059261126291719]nearest-neighbor and bilinear HRTF interpolation[/url].

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27920370/cfd92f4f6caea906e7018969626186fa10562a5b.png[/img]

[h1]Direct-Sound Occlusion[/h1]

UE4 provides a raycast occlusion solution by default. In 4.16, occlusion plugins can handle how direct sound is occluded on a per-source basis. Users control the processing with [i]Occlusion Plugin Settings[/i] assets. The Steam Audio plugin lets users choose between raycast and partial occlusion, and whether to apply physics-based attenuation.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27920370/b1adf80430b5cbcd0df9fbb33e1d757969b6d02b.png[/img]

[h1]Physically-based Sound Propagation[/h1]

UE4 allows users to author reverbs using traditional reverb volumes. In 4.16, reverb plugins can efficiently apply convolution reverb to mixed audio and customize how reverbs are generated and applied on a per-source basis. Users control the processing with [i]Reverb Plugin Settings[/i] assets. The Steam Audio plugin lets users choose between realtime and baked sound propagation and configure a mixing fraction. Steam Audio also allows users to apply a globally-configured listener-centric reverb.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27920370/bd8faca0719a3c5dde548c9d49aa364e20c1ec19.png[/img]

This portion of Steam Audio is what many users are going to be most excited about. We've introduced a variety of new actors and components that handle tagging acoustically meaningful geometry, specifying acoustic materials, and creating acoustic probes for baking sound propagation data. We've extended the UI in ways that should be familiar to UE4 users. In the same way that you use the Build menu to bake lightmap information, you can now find a button for baking listener-centric reverb. Finally, we have a robust set of globally-configurable settings to customize quality and performance.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27920370/5f46ca7f18a87d0a31f59ea4f1ecb55f20510e2f.png[/img][img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27920370/0f5dbf09c288f510214e9cc670e715e67bb23bea.png[/img]

notes.title: Destinations: The Quest Update
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5519564/0a07def5966d122c61425059551604376f5c2ca7.png[/img]

Complete quests, collect souvenirs, and stick them to your head! The Quest Update to [url=store.steampowered.com/app/453170]Destinations[/url] is here, with a host of new features and content to explore.

[h1]Introducing Geocaching Quests[/h1]

Travel to various Destinations to find hidden item caches using the new Cache Finder tool. Locate one, and you (along with anyone questing with you) will earn a wearable item or avatar head to customize the way you look. Fancy a different hat than the one you found? Trade with other Destinations players on Steam or head over to the Steam Market. A new set of geocaching quests will appear each week, so get out there and find some caches!

[video=autoplay preload loop poster=http://media.steampowered.com/apps/453170/announcements/quest_update/quest_update_video1_thumb.jpg]http://media.steampowered.com/apps/453170/announcements/quest_update/quest_update_video1.webm?v=1[/video]

[h1]New Avatar Options[/h1]

Show off your sense of style with new avatar customization options. You can now place hats, hair, and other wearables (which you’ve found on various quests) on your head. Resize and recolor every item to your taste, then save the whole set as a preset outfit for quick access.

[h1]New Destinations, Tools, and More[/h1]

Two new official Destinations have arrived: ponder the cosmos in the Clockwork Orrery, or enjoy a relaxing stay on the water at Illia’s Retreat. With the addition of tools, like the Airbrush and Drone Controller, players have new ways to interact with the world and other players. We’ve also added new avatar heads, avatar hands (complete with gestures of course), and a refreshed interface which makes it easier to meet up with friends in Destinations.

[video=autoplay preload loop poster=http://media.steampowered.com/apps/453170/announcements/quest_update/quest_update_video2_thumb.jpg]http://media.steampowered.com/apps/453170/announcements/quest_update/quest_update_video2.webm?v=1[/video]
[i]Ballooninator vs Pop Zapper[/i]

[video=autoplay preload loop poster=http://media.steampowered.com/apps/453170/announcements/quest_update/quest_update_video3_thumb.jpg]http://media.steampowered.com/apps/453170/announcements/quest_update/quest_update_video3.webm?v=1[/video]
[i]Collaborate in multiplayer with the Airbrush tool[/i]

[video=autoplay preload loop poster=http://media.steampowered.com/apps/453170/announcements/quest_update/quest_update_video4_thumb.jpg]http://media.steampowered.com/apps/453170/announcements/quest_update/quest_update_video4.webm?v=1[/video]
[i]Take control of the skies with the Drone Controller[/i]

Whether you're using a Vive, Rift, or any other OpenVR compatible headset there's never been a better time to book a tour in Destinations. [i](Motion controllers are required for Quests, Tools, Props, and Wearables)[/i].

As always, let us know what you think in the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/453170/discussions]discussion[/url] boards.

notes.title: SteamVR Updated (1485391631)
notes.content:
SteamVR has been updated with the following changes. This is the same build that went into the beta on January 25th 
 
General:
[list]
[*]Added a new transition UI that appears when an application is starting, stopping, or not currently rendering. In some applications it will appear during level transitions.
[*]Added a new system skybox that shows when an application is running but not rendering instead of the user’s configured skybox (and environment.) The user’s skybox and environment will still show when no application is running.
[*]Fixed many cases of application icons not appearing in the Now Playing section of the dashboard.
[*]Fixed SteamVR crash on exit
[*]MessageOverlay is now modal.
[*]Fixed a class of compositor errors not getting promoted properly to SteamVR status UI.
[*]Fixes for SteamVR graceful recovery on some cases of late HMD connectivity.
[*]Fixed crash that could happen on SteamVR startup
[*]Fixed vrpathreg error when running on a clean machine that has never has the Visual Studio 2013 C Runtime installed.
[*]Fix for crash related to unmatched VR_Init/VR_Shutdown calls.
[/list]

notes.title: Scaling the Play Area
notes.content:
Today we have a guest blog post from Andy Moore at Radial Games, one of the  companies behind [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/386690/]Fantastic Contraption[/url].

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5519564/33ad7ce5ef7d6475092635c9bd0edd36a0867248.jpg[/img]

A few days ago we released [url=http://northwaygames.com/contraption-kaiju-update/]Fantastic Contraption v1.5: The Kaiju Update[/url]. The update's key feature is the ability to rescale the entire play space so that you can tower over the levels like a lizard over Tokyo. Why and how did we do this? First, we have to explore the reasons behind the initial scale of the game.


[H1]The Benefit Of Room Scale Design[/H1]

Fantastic Contraption was built from the ground-up to be a 360-degree room-scale experience - one that uses your entire room and requires you to move and turn around. There were two primary reasons for this; the first (and most obvious) reason was simply that the Vive was the just-announced hot-new-product and we were excited to push our new toy to its limits.

The second reason was that, at room-scale, our in-game actions trigger proprioception queues in your body. Your body uses proprioception to feed your body extra data about your environment; for example, there are nerves in your neck that help you feel a sense of awe when you look up at a skyscraper; those nerves don't fire when you look at a photograph of the same skyscraper, so those feel like different experiences to you. Building a large contraption that fills your living room triggers these various physiological reactions, and we believe any game that fully leverages these queues will - by default - feel more real than any game that ignores them. We love the sense of room-filling majesty a large contraption can invoke in players; we love that players have to duck under connecting beams, step over oddly spaced wheels, dodge windmill arms, and inch back cautiously from catapults. These all add to the experience in a very real (if hard to measure) sense.

Being able to forget our mundane reality and being transported to Fantastic new environments was key for us, and room-scale technology really made that easier to achieve.


[H1]The Challenge Of Room Scale Design[/H1]

There are two big problems with room-scale design though. First, simply not all games fit the format; many experiences would work just as well seated, standing, and sometimes even as a flat game not requiring VR at all. Thankfully we designed the game from day one to be room-scale and didn't have to wrestle with this one.

The second problem is accessibility. To play Fantastic Contraption we required you had a large play area and an able body. In some cultures, tiny living spaces is the norm, and entire markets were cut off from us. People that lacked flexibility in their joints, the elderly, the wheelchair-bound, the people with their leg in a cast, and the disabled in general - we were leaving them out in the cold. Finally, let us not forget those anguished souls among us who choose to stay less mobile when gaming. We get it, you had a long day! Maybe you want to relax and get off your feet!

When we considered how many people were missing out on building Fantastic Contraptions, it gave us sad faces. We made the decision that while Fantastic Contraption was /best/ played room-scale, /requiring/ it was unfair.

[H1]Planning The Change[/H1]

We wanted the game to be whimsical, fun, and cute - but fit the play space of as many people as possible. Our goal was clear, but the path to obtain it was quite murky. Could we take our already-implemented "grabby claw" and make the game work from a universal standing position? Could we just bring all the interaction elements closer to the player? Could we do clever level design to make everything just work with minimal changes?

Soon after the initial launch of the game, we put a few "experimental" buttons in the Settings menu and let people change their play space to test these ideas out. We built some presets for seated and standing modes that people could play with and made some minor edits to see if this kind of gameplay had legs.

It turns out that didn't work so well. All the effort we put into making things feel big, your play area feeling uncluttered, open, and relaxing - all went out the window when we started crowding things up against you. Editing objects far away was annoying. Sometimes a person's desk would prevent them from reaching the floor; sometimes people would "lose" an object by accidentally placing it behind them and never turning around, or even just placing it under their chair or inside their couch. We needed a different solution.

After a lot of multiplayer meetings on the green of [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/425720/]Cloudlands: VR Minigolf[/url], we came up with the idea of having two primary modes: the standard room-scale mode, and a second "scaled" mode where you stand /beside/ the play area and can scale, rotate, raise/lower, and otherwise place the game wherever you want.

[H1]Custom Scaling - The Killer Solution[/H1]

Because we allow you to set the height, size, placement, and rotation of the play area, we ended up solving a lot of problems in one fell swoop. You could now quickly size the area to fit on your lap for seated play, or you could scale it up fairly large and sit cross-legged on your floor to play. You could align it beside you so you don't clip the tea on the edge of your desk or set it up for someone in a wheelchair. You can make a "mini room scale" configuration that allows shorter humans to feel like they are ten feet tall. You can make your play area face your tracking device head-on for better visibility. This scaling solution ended up being very customizable, and therefore very flexible for just about every situation.

So flexible, in fact, that this change also made the game hardware-agnostic. As long as you have tracked hands, the game would now work well with any modern VR hardware with any space restriction you might have. From a business angle, making this change was a no-brainer.

This scaling solution put an ace up our sleeve as well. We often struggled with how we'd implement a level editor - when by definition the level exists outside of your reachable play space. With the scaling solution now implemented, getting the player within arm's reach of any corner of the level was trivial. Implementing a scaled mode of play made the level editor possible, and now we're wishing we built this feature first for our own use! (Our next big patch will contain the level editor for everyone to enjoy.)


[H1]Challenges[/H1]

Implementing this wasn't exactly easy and required a lot of re-design. Now that the player was standing, looming, over each of our levels, we realized they were potentially standing inside level geometry; all of our levels had to be touched up, and some had to be mirrored or flipped to ensure there was always safe standing space. We had to worry about things (like text or save-game-models) being visible when scaled down, tutorial fonts and placements had to be reworked, and we redesigned the helmet-world entirely to fit the new paradigm.

Then there’s the interface. Figuring out exactly how to scale the world with such flexibility in 3D space took a lot of brainpower and iterations. Tons of work all around. We're now over 6 months from our initial launch and we just now felt comfortable enough to release the feature! We learned our lesson, though - start early. Plan for this eventuality.

notes.title: Scaling the Play Area
notes.content:
Today we have a guest blog post from Andy Moore at Radial Games, one of the  companies behind [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/386690/]Fantastic Contraption[/url].

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5519564/33ad7ce5ef7d6475092635c9bd0edd36a0867248.jpg[/img]

A few days ago we released [url=http://northwaygames.com/contraption-kaiju-update/]Fantastic Contraption v1.5: The Kaiju Update[/url]. The update's key feature is the ability to rescale the entire play space so that you can tower over the levels like a lizard over Tokyo. Why and how did we do this? First, we have to explore the reasons behind the initial scale of the game.


[H1]The Benefit Of Room Scale Design[/H1]

Fantastic Contraption was built from the ground-up to be a 360-degree room-scale experience - one that uses your entire room and requires you to move and turn around. There were two primary reasons for this; the first (and most obvious) reason was simply that the Vive was the just-announced hot-new-product and we were excited to push our new toy to its limits.

The second reason was that, at room-scale, our in-game actions trigger proprioception queues in your body. Your body uses proprioception to feed your body extra data about your environment; for example, there are nerves in your neck that help you feel a sense of awe when you look up at a skyscraper; those nerves don't fire when you look at a photograph of the same skyscraper, so those feel like different experiences to you. Building a large contraption that fills your living room triggers these various physiological reactions, and we believe any game that fully leverages these queues will - by default - feel more real than any game that ignores them. We love the sense of room-filling majesty a large contraption can invoke in players; we love that players have to duck under connecting beams, step over oddly spaced wheels, dodge windmill arms, and inch back cautiously from catapults. These all add to the experience in a very real (if hard to measure) sense.

Being able to forget our mundane reality and being transported to Fantastic new environments was key for us, and room-scale technology really made that easier to achieve.


[H1]The Challenge Of Room Scale Design[/H1]

There are two big problems with room-scale design though. First, simply not all games fit the format; many experiences would work just as well seated, standing, and sometimes even as a flat game not requiring VR at all. Thankfully we designed the game from day one to be room-scale and didn't have to wrestle with this one.

The second problem is accessibility. To play Fantastic Contraption we required you had a large play area and an able body. In some cultures, tiny living spaces is the norm, and entire markets were cut off from us. People that lacked flexibility in their joints, the elderly, the wheelchair-bound, the people with their leg in a cast, and the disabled in general - we were leaving them out in the cold. Finally, let us not forget those anguished souls among us who choose to stay less mobile when gaming. We get it, you had a long day! Maybe you want to relax and get off your feet!

When we considered how many people were missing out on building Fantastic Contraptions, it gave us sad faces. We made the decision that while Fantastic Contraption was /best/ played room-scale, /requiring/ it was unfair.

[H1]Planning The Change[/H1]

We wanted the game to be whimsical, fun, and cute - but fit the play space of as many people as possible. Our goal was clear, but the path to obtain it was quite murky. Could we take our already-implemented "grabby claw" and make the game work from a universal standing position? Could we just bring all the interaction elements closer to the player? Could we do clever level design to make everything just work with minimal changes?

Soon after the initial launch of the game, we put a few "experimental" buttons in the Settings menu and let people change their play space to test these ideas out. We built some presets for seated and standing modes that people could play with and made some minor edits to see if this kind of gameplay had legs.

It turns out that didn't work so well. All the effort we put into making things feel big, your play area feeling uncluttered, open, and relaxing - all went out the window when we started crowding things up against you. Editing objects far away was annoying. Sometimes a person's desk would prevent them from reaching the floor; sometimes people would "lose" an object by accidentally placing it behind them and never turning around, or even just placing it under their chair or inside their couch. We needed a different solution.

After a lot of multiplayer meetings on the green of [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/425720/]Cloudlands: VR Minigolf[/url], we came up with the idea of having two primary modes: the standard room-scale mode, and a second "scaled" mode where you stand /beside/ the play area and can scale, rotate, raise/lower, and otherwise place the game wherever you want.

[H1]Custom Scaling - The Killer Solution[/H1]

Because we allow you to set the height, size, placement, and rotation of the play area, we ended up solving a lot of problems in one fell swoop. You could now quickly size the area to fit on your lap for seated play, or you could scale it up fairly large and sit cross-legged on your floor to play. You could align it beside you so you don't clip the tea on the edge of your desk or set it up for someone in a wheelchair. You can make a "mini room scale" configuration that allows shorter humans to feel like they are ten feet tall. You can make your play area face your tracking device head-on for better visibility. This scaling solution ended up being very customizable, and therefore very flexible for just about every situation.

So flexible, in fact, that this change also made the game hardware-agnostic. As long as you have tracked hands, the game would now work well with any modern VR hardware with any space restriction you might have. From a business angle, making this change was a no-brainer.

This scaling solution put an ace up our sleeve as well. We often struggled with how we'd implement a level editor - when by definition the level exists outside of your reachable play space. With the scaling solution now implemented, getting the player within arm's reach of any corner of the level was trivial. Implementing a scaled mode of play made the level editor possible, and now we're wishing we built this feature first for our own use! (Our next big patch will contain the level editor for everyone to enjoy.)


[H1]Challenges[/H1]

Implementing this wasn't exactly easy and required a lot of re-design. Now that the player was standing, looming, over each of our levels, we realized they were potentially standing inside level geometry; all of our levels had to be touched up, and some had to be mirrored or flipped to ensure there was always safe standing space. We had to worry about things (like text or save-game-models) being visible when scaled down, tutorial fonts and placements had to be reworked, and we redesigned the helmet-world entirely to fit the new paradigm.

Then there’s the interface. Figuring out exactly how to scale the world with such flexibility in 3D space took a lot of brainpower and iterations. Tons of work all around. We're now over 6 months from our initial launch and we just now felt comfortable enough to release the feature! We learned our lesson, though - start early. Plan for this eventuality.

It's definitely worth it, though. We encourage all developers to make a flexible, accessible design - not just for your users, but for your game's and studio's own health as well. VR is a new market, and every little edge you get is a foothold that will keep your studio (and the whole ecosystem!) afloat for the coming years. Use everything in your toolbox! Limiting your game to one niche of customers is dangerous!

If you're starting fresh, think of all these eventualities up front. Changing everything after the fact was hard (as we learned!), but engineering for this from day one isn't a lot of extra work.

And for the gamers out there - we're excited that everybody has a chance to try out our game, regardless of their mobility or real-estate limitations.

Let's make something Fantastic!

notes.title: SteamVR Updated (1479163853)
notes.content:
SteamVR has been updated with the following changes:
 
General:
[list]
[*]SteamVR status window can now be minimized (with setting to minimize to tray).
[*]Updated VRFrames.csv to include new frame data related to async mode.
[*]Fixed a bug preventing HMD system button presses from being recognized.
[/list]
 
Compositor:
[list]
[*]Asynchronous reprojection support.*
[*]Added dome projection controls for compositor background images.
[*]Fix for right eye occasionally showing left image in some rare cases (GL specific).
[/list]
 
Vive-specific:
[list]
[*]Added night-mode (activate using button in dashboard settings).
[*]Minor improvement to chromatic aberration correction.
[*]Fixed blue fringing or flashing at the periphery reported by some users.
[*]Patch for purple ghosting on 10-series NVIDIA cards using driver v375.XX.
[*]Bluetooth driver install now uses force option to fix broken installs.
[*]Updated vivelink.exe (v1.0.49.0) and vivebtdriver.exe (v12.0.1.102).
[*]Vivelink - Fixed 4 digit BT driver version query problem.
[*]Vivelink - Improved BLE connect reliability.
[*]ViveBTDriver - Auto recover BT driver when BT USB stuck.
[*]ViveBTDriver - Fix for Win8.1 WU update problem.
[/list]
 
* Notes on async reprojection:
[olist]
[*]Requires Nvidia driver version 372.54 or newer.
[*]AMD not supported in this version.
[*]Can be disabled in SteamVR settings under Performance by unchecking "Allow asynchronous reprojection".
[*]Current status is listed in the lower left section of SteamVR Settings (Async Reprojection On/Off).  If you have "Allow asynchronous reprojection" checked, but are still seeing Async Reprojection Off on the left, this means it is not supported on your current setup - see above for requirements.
[*]Frame timing graph has been updated to show the number of times each frame has been presented (white line in the stacked cpu graph) and the number of times each frame has been reprojected to a different vsync than originally rendered for (red line on the stacked gpu graph).
[*]"Allow interleaved reprojection" checkbox still applies in async mode.  It controls whether the application is dropped to 45hz when not making framerate, or if it is allowed to get further and further behind until a frame winds up getting presented twice.  This leads to less positional judder, but that judder is more random (which tends to be more annoying).
[/olist]

notes.title: Destinations: Music, Cannons, and More
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25293420/e0d669e11583dc2dccd44aa4b953515ee24831ce.png[/img]

Today we are updating [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/453170/]Destinations[/url] with great new content to explore, a simplified user interface, and new scripting hooks for content creators. With this update, players and creators can get even more out of Destinations.

[h1]New Content[/h1]
We are adding three new Destinations to the default shipped set: 
[b]Jam Session:[/b] Play the guitar, drums, and marimba with friends in this Liverpool inspired bar.
[b]Tower Bridge:[/b] Explore the bank of Thames River next to London’s famous Tower Bridge. 
[b]Cannon Wars:[/b] Destroy your opponent’s fortifications before they destroy yours – your cannon fires cannonballs, mines, or anything else you throw in (beach balls, pumpkins, cake…)

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5519564/a61c0f1cbf8f61b4b3abd86bab177a2995bb689d.png[/img]

In addition, we’re adding more unlockable props and a new avatar – explore the new content and the Destinations Workshop to unlock them all! (Prop support is only available for players with motion controllers)

[h1]New User Interface[/h1]
We’ve added new features to the user interface to make it easier to find content and hang out with friends in Destinations.  A new dashboard makes it simpler to see where you are, what you can do, and what’s new. This updated interface also allows players to browse popular Destinations from the Workshop and subscribe to them in the menu. In addition, the UI has been tweaked to make it easier to host a room, join a room, and quickly see who the host of the room is. 

[h1]From the Workshop[/h1]
The Destinations Workshop continues to grow, and as always we are impressed with what the community has created in 3D or captured with photogrammetry. Special callout to Jane Ng of Campo Santo for her [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=779320862]Firewatch[/url] Destination – it  has quickly become one of the most popular Destinations in the Workshop, and offers a unique opportunity to enter a game world in VR. Other notable additions to the Workshop include ianl’s [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=778182111]The Banquet[/url], and ATAT_Carleton’s multiple [url=http://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/?id=780691539]UK Heritage Site[/url] photogrammetry captures.

[url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=779320862][img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5519564/1f6700d0559cb6cd38fb3761c19f08597788cdf6.jpg[/img][/url]

[h1]For Creators[/h1]
This update also includes additional hooks for content creators and scripters. We won’t get into the details here, but it boils down to making it simpler to set hand attachments and trigger interactions with hands. For more info on these changes, check out the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/453170/announcements/detail/527312385585770159]change notes[/url] for this update. We’ve also updated the [url=https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Destinations]Destinations Wiki[/url] with more documentation and tutorials about using Destinations Workshop Tools.

[url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/453170/]Destinations[/url] is available for free on Steam, and is compatible with any HMD that is supported by OpenVR, including the HTC Vive and Oculus Rift. Let us know what you think in the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/453170/discussions/]Destinations forums[/url].

[/olist]

If you get an error about missing files after this update, try relaunching Steam.

notes.title: Destinations: Public Lobbies and More
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5519564/46cbd9494ced5b9796f1a4ebd8111e1c7c656b1e.png[/img]

Today we are adding Public Lobbies to [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/453170/]Destinations[/url]. Now it’s even easier to meet with players around the world and explore Destinations together in VR. In addition, we are shipping more default Destinations, props, and tutorials for players to dig into and learn from.

[h1]Public Lobbies[/h1]
Join players from around the world with the new Public Lobbies feature. Meet new people, customize your avatar, and interact with physics props. Make new friends and add them as Steam friends from inside of Destinations. All players can create a public lobby from any Destination on the Steam Workshop - simply select "Create Lobby" from the Social panel and it will show up in the public lobby list.

[h1]New Content[/h1]
In addition, we are adding three new Destinations to the default set of shipped Destinations: photogrammetry of the Valve office lobby, La Pedrera in Barcelona, and Arcade Toss, a multiplayer game built in Destinations. We are also including a set of new props, a new avatar, and new hand gestures. Some of these items are locked by default though – you will need to explore different Destinations in order to unlock each unique prop. (Prop and hand gesture support is only available for players with motion controllers)

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5519564/dae3713360559030d4d37cfdddb2f15d2e14169c.png[/img]

[h1]More Examples and Documentation[/h1]
To accompany the new content, we’ve added two new articles to the [url=https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Destinations]Destinations Wiki[/url]. One is an extensive tutorial on [url=https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Destinations/Advanced_Indoors_Photogrammetry]indoor photogrammetry[/url] which walks through the creation of the Valve Lobby Destination. The other document shows how [url=https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Destinations/Scripting]scripting[/url] was used with Destinations in order to create the Arcade Toss Destination. All of the content assets for Arcade Toss will be shipped with this update as well.

[h1]Workshop[/h1]
We’ve been very excited to see the great content that creators have continued to upload. 120 Destinations have been uploaded to date, allowing players to visit 10 different countries. In addition there are numerous Destinations that depict game settings and other fictional places. A few notable mentions: mkhamra for his beautiful photogrammetry captures of [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=761080905]Jordan[/url], ToitagL for his capture of [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=755338731]South Corsica[/url], peppels for his capture of his [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=735095640]Studio Room[/url], and Rectus for his [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=735164875]Beach Sunset[/url] Destination. 

Destinations is compatible with any HMD that is supported by OpenVR, including the HTC Vive and Oculus Rift. It is available for free on Steam, and you can  [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/453170/]get it here[/url].

notes.title: Update Update Update
notes.content:
[img]http://store.steampowered.com/gfxproxy/apps/418650/ss_90ba555e3d6b55849b3d9ce7925209d747a6ee04.1920x1080.jpg?t=1473786325[/img]
When we discuss business with VR developers on what works in VR, we tell them the same things that works in 2D games.  Make a good game, price it right, listen to your community and update, update, update.

The cycle of update, feedback, update is an important one in the development of a game.  Today with [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/418650/]Space Pirate Trainer[/url]’s massive update we are seeing that again. Already one of the most popular VR titles on Steam, today’s massive update paired with a 3-day sale at 25% off,  will introduce even more players to the game and give existing players more competition on the leader boards.

Other titles that have been doing significant updates that you might want to go back and reconsider if you haven’t already picked them up:

[url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/451840/]Out of Ammo [/url]
Out of Ammo started with the rough outline of its gameplay and world and continued to refine both with every one of its updates and now RocketWerkz actually has its [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/451840/allnews/]release candidate[/url] available to play now.  If you didn’t try it when it first came out – it has changed! Jump in, play, and give feedback.


[url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/425720/]Cloudlands VR Minigolf[/url] 
Futuretown wasn’t content with just bug-fixes but months after release have come out with a course editor update.  [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/425720/workshop/]Their workshop[/url] already has over 200 courses created and shared!  Still not sure? They also have a demo available.

[url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/322770/]Vanishing Realms[/url] 
There are significant updates and then there are massive updates – Indimo just released a [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/322770/announcements/detail/582476480908611712]massive update[/url] on its RPG that had already been met with Overwhelmingly Positive reviews.  It just keeps getting better.

[url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/269170/]Pool Nation VR[/url]
How do you update a pool game that already nailed the playing pool part of the game?  Cherry Pop Games added darts, skreeball, and air hockey.  How did they choose those games?  They asked the community and they answered.  A great loop of update, feedback, update, feedback.

[url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/436320/]Raw Data[/url]
When Survios‘s Raw Data jumped to #1 on the Steam Charts with their release into Early Access you might think that was it – mission accomplished.  Their work was done.  Far from it.  They continue [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/436320/allnews/]regular updates[/url] adding content, fixing bugs, and regular events with the community.  

[url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/380220/]Hover Junkers[/url]
Stress Level Zero didn’t let early success go to their heads, they continue updating Hover Junkers regularly.  Not only did they add a [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/380220/announcements/detail/577965688891786458]co-op mode[/url], just last week they added new weapons.

This list could continue for pages.  We see games like [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/484870/]Battledome[/url], [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/435490/]Pierhead Arcade[/url], [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/457550/]BigScreen[/url], [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/471710/]Rec Room[/url], and more keep updating, getting feedback, and updating again.  So make sure to go back and check out earlier titles to see if they tickle your fancy now… and if we missed listing your favorite update – list it below.

notes.title: Destinations: Multiplayer Update
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5519564/7152e51ca139fab53807b06a636a813a46635088.jpg[/img]

Today we are adding Multiplayer to Destinations. Players can now invite, join, and chat with their friends while exploring different Destinations. In addition, we’ve added the ability to customize avatars and bring physics props in the world.

[h1]Multiplayer[/h1]
Players can now see which friends are online with the new Friends panel in the Destinations Menu. From here they can invite friends to join their Destination, or request to join the friend at theirs. Once in the same Destination, players will be able to voice chat with everyone who has joined.

[h1]Avatars[/h1]
What’s multiplayer without customizable avatars? In this release we’ve included a set of simple avatar heads and a couple avatar hands to choose from. Once you pick an avatar you can customize it using the new Avatar panel in the Menu.

[h1]Props[/h1]
Destinations now ships with a set of props that players will be able to create, scale up or down, and toss around. This feature is currently only available for users with motion controls. 

We’d also like to take a moment to acknowledge all the creators who have contributed to the Destinations Workshop so far. From the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=708849136]interior of a watermill[/url] to a [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=702918403]view from space[/url], we’ve been excited to see the work of our community’s creators. One standout submission is from Croteam, who recreated a level from their game The Talos Principle in [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=724619397]stunning detail[/url].

[url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/453170]Destinations[/url] is available for free on Steam, and is compatible with any HMD that is supported by OpenVR, including the HTC Vive and Oculus Rift.

Let us know what you think in the Destinations forums:
http://steamcommunity.com/app/453170/discussions/

notes.title: SteamVR Updated (1469551863)
notes.content:
SteamVR has been updated with the following changes.

General:
[list]
[*]Fixed “Failed to terminate 'vrserver.exe'” error that happens occasionally on SteamVR startup.
[*]Fixed in-VR notifications so they will start appearing again.
[*]SteamVR will now start automatically when a Vive controller is turned on, a controller’s system button is pressed, or the button on a Vive headset is pressed. Steam must be running for this feature to work.
[*]Fixed case where starting Steam while SteamVR was running could cause tracking to stop working.
[*]Fixed an issue where controller hand assignment would not happen right away when launching a game with the headset and controllers idle.
[/list]

Compositor:
[list]
[*]Added debug output to back buffer for per-frame debugging.  Select Developer Mode from drop-down menu in mirror window, then toggle using F8.
[/list]

HTC Vive:
[list]
[*]Fixed issue with the left eye on some HTC Vive headsets showing a solid color when turning back on after being idle.
[*]Fixed issue with HMD panels turning off briefly and then immediately turning back on. This could happen when the proximity sensor wasn’t being activated but the headset was in motion.
[*] Fixed issue with base station management to check for Bluetooth when it is not enabled
[*] Added firmware upgrade for base station Bluetooth connectivity to improve power management
[*] Fixed problems with base station power management
[/list]

VR Dashboard:
[list]
[*]Added settings to control the amount of time the system must be idle for displays and controllers to automatically turn off.
[*]Added a setting to shut down SteamVR automatically after being idle for a specified length of time.
[*] Moved the setting to turn off controllers when SteamVR exits from the desktop to the dashboard
[/list]

notes.title: SteamVR and Audio Technologies
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5519564/de977aec5f87cf15ce472e5fab6f2c8a12810479.jpg[/img]

High quality audio is a very important component in most media experiences, and especially so in VR. Spatial audio (audio appearing to come from a specific location in the environment) in VR and 3D games can be critical for immersion, presence and conveyance of information for game play and storytelling.

The way we experience sound in the real world involves many factors: the source of the sound, its location and distance relative to the listener’s location and orientation, the shape and geometry surrounding the sound source and listener, as well as the listener’s body, head, ear shapes and perhaps most importantly, the human brain.
 
Virtual projects can differ widely in the sound variables they need to simulate, as can listener preferences. For instance, simulating geometry based sound occlusion and reflections may be very important for a VR experience that requires traversal through a dense interior environment, but perhaps less important for VR experiences that take place in a single scene, or primarily in an outdoor environment. Likewise, high resolution binaural rendering for a single sound source might be useful for cues that need to make the player face a certain direction, but less important for ambient sound sources, or sound sources that are coupled with an easily identifiable visual element.  Some socially focused VR projects may decide it’s important to support stereo or surround sound speaker playback, as well as stereo headphones. 

We believe that promoting a growing range of research and technology in this area will enable developers to use the best audio technology for their needs, as well as help drive innovation in the future among 3D audio providers. 

To help out, we have tested and are showcasing below (in no particular order), a selection of cutting-edge 3D audio technologies ready to use within 3D game engines and SteamVR. We think you’ll find this list interesting, educational and hopefully useful in your quest for creating and playing the best VR audio experiences possible.


[h1]VR Audio Enhancement[/h1]

[url=https://www.impulsonic.com/] Impulsonic	[/url]
Impulsonic’s Phonon is a fully featured set of physics-based audio tools for creating immersive environmental audio effects. Phonon includes single source and channel based binaural processing, propagated geometry based reflections, dynamic reverb and occlusion based on scene geometry. Compatible with existing game engines and middleware (Unity, Unreal, Fmod, Wwise), Phonon plugs into existing workflows, and provides multi-platform based performance throttling for low latency and easy deployment.

[url=http://realspace3daudio.com/rs3d-steamvr/] Visisonics	[/url]
Visisonics’ RS3D is the result of on 15+ years of leading research by University of Maryland scientists. RS3D utilizes a physics based reverb/propagation engine, proprietary HRTFs, scalable level of detail for targeting multiple platforms, assignable room materials and personalized HRTF integration. Supporting major game engines and middleware, RS3D also fits most current workflows.

[url=http://www.dolby.com/us/en/professional/content-creation/vr.html] Dolby	[/url]
Dolby’s Atmos is an n-channel, “object based sound” format that has been widely adopted by traditional cinemas and is now available for the home consumer looking to expand their speaker arrays skyward to add a vertical component to their sound experience. As a format, Atmos also dovetails nicely into linear VR, 3D game and room-scale VR production providing an end to end solution with creation tools, distribution formats and rendering solutions for everything from an array of speakers to headphones.

[url=https://developer.oculus.com/documentation/audiosdk/latest/] Oculus Audio SDK	[/url]
Oculus licensed and refined early spatialization algorithms developed by Visisonics, making them development ready for most major engines and audio middleware. The result is an effective free plugin for achieving enhanced 3D sound and is available via the Oculus SDK.

[url=http://www.twobigears.com/spatworks/#features] Two Big Ears	[/url]
Although recently acquired by Facebook, Two Big Ears still offer a free 360 video audio workstation which includes multi-channel recording, authored soundscapes, ambisonic playback, single sound source binarual rendering, htlm5 integration, streaming and interactivity.

[url=http://newaudiotechnology.com/] New Audio Technology	[/url]
N.A.T offers a range of tools for creating 3D sound experiences including tools for linear DAW based production monitoring / mixdown of current and future n-channel format types for film and music, SAGE audio engine for in-game/vr spatial virtualization and a virtual device driver that takes 5.1/7.1 output and virtualizes it to stereo headphone mix.

[url=http://dts.com] DTS	[/url]
DTS offers a host of 3D sound tools/encoders and playback/decoder systems ranging from n-channel speaker systems to headphones, managing early calibration through to the listener's environment. They offer a wifi based home speaker system for easily placing speakers, full n-channel->n-channel down/upmixing as well as streaming n-channel encoded audio among other features.

[url=http://www.ossic.com] OSSIC	[/url]
OSSIC has developed the OSSIC X, a consumer facing multi-driver 3D headphone that utilizes software models and physical speakers to render 5.1/7.1 and n-channel formats to locations relative to the listener’s head. It uses its own head tracking to calibrate to certain aspects of the listeners physique as well as using the listener’s own ears by playing from locations mimicking those of the virtual locations. It can utilize SteamVR tracking data, its own head tracking or combine its own tracking with game camera orientation. Software versions of their technology are also forthcoming.

[url=http://thesubpac.com/] SubPac	[/url]
We don’t only hear sound through the holes in our ears, we also feel it on our skin and as it radiates through our bones and bodies especially where bass is concerned. SubPac offers wearable sub-woofer technology for VR consumers looking to experience low frequencies that are often lost in headphone based experiences.


[h1]3D Audio Fundamentals - New to VR development? These solutions will enable effective 3D object based sound for VR, as well as host most of 3D sound enhancement plugins listed above.[/h1]

[b]Unity and Unreal Game Engines[/b]
Most current VR experiences are being created with one of these engines, both of which come complete with an array of tools for implementing effective 3D sound. As long as the virtual microphone or “listener” is attached to the SteamVR player game camera, head tracking in VR will automatically pan and attenuate sounds correctly depending on where the player is looking.  Looking at the tools available in your engine is a great place to start learning the basics of 3D audio and may provide most of what you need. Both Unity and Unreal also support audio middleware such as Wwise and Fmod as well as most of the spatialization technologies listed here.
[url=http://unity3d.com/] Unity[/url]
[url=https://www.unrealengine.com/] Unreal[/url]

[b]Wwise and FMOD Audio Engines[/b]
Both of these products are relatively ubiquitous audio middleware made for handling all aspects of game audio. As VR audio design and implementation is often very similar to that of 3D games, their tool-sets are still applicable and powerful when working in VR. They’ve also started adding various VR target tools to their collection and support some of the spatialization plugins listed here.
[url=http://www.fmod.org/] Fmod[/url]
[url=https://www.audiokinetic.com/products/wwise-vr/] Wwise[/url]

Have feedback? Let us know in the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/250820/discussions/]SteamVR Discussions[/url].

notes.title: The Lab: Appliance of Science Update
notes.content:
[url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/450390/][img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/23034005/c373cd6d3e6a3aa12c9e4732258291f750631e62.png[/img][/url]

What's science without a little competition? Why, it's barely science at all! That's why we applied some science to The Lab and created the Appliance of Science Update, introducing a spirit of bloodthirsty competition to the world of ethically questionable research.

Now you can compete with your fellow test subjects on the new [url=http://steamcommunity.com/stats/450390/leaderboards/1267291/]global leaderboards[/url] for Longbow, Xortex, and Slingshot, and prove to the world that you're the best at science. But hold on to your grant money, because we didn't stop there. We've also made a bunch of gameplay adjustments to all three games.

Longbow now features an unlimited number of enemy waves, along with a new scoring system to reward slaying enemies, nailing headshots, popping balloons, and more. Each successive wave includes more enemies, who will move faster and have an increased chance of wearing armor. Your exploding barrels and oil cauldrons reset every eight waves, so be sure to use them!

Xortex now offers a brand new way to play, Xortex Infinite, with progressively more frantic action as you maneuver your drone to collect powerups, increasing your score multiplier while gunning down enemies. Xortex Infinite also replaces the Laser with a powerful Bomb, which destroys all nearby threats. Use it wisely, however--detonating your Bomb also resets your score multiplier.

Finally, the rebalanced Slingshot will present you with new core calibration career opportunities. Wipe out the Aperture Storage annex with bigger, better barrel explosions, as well as a host of scoring adjustments to help you solidify your place as a world class calibrator.

Speaking of world class, the Appliance of Science Update also adds support for subtitles and text localization, along with a host of other additions and improvements. You can read all about those in the patch notes.

[url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/450390/announcements/detail/686051181258823394]The Appliance of Science Update[/url] is now included in The Lab, available for free on Steam. So strap on your headset, grab your Nobel Prize or other favorite blunt object, and populate those leaderboards with your own empirical data, for science!
